sources.title: George Lusztig, Introduction to Quantum Groups (Progress in Mathematics 110, Birkhauser 1993; second printing 1994), author-hosted scan
sources.locator: Ch. 1, §1.2.3-1.2.15, printed pp. 4-9 (inner product on the free algebra, radical and quotient f, skew derivations r_i, separation 1.2.15); Ch. 23, §23.1.1-23.2.2, printed pp. 185-188 (modified algebra, divided powers, identity 23.1.3(6), A-form and A-basis); Ch. 31, §31.1, printed pp. 245-246 (change-of-rings form); Ch. 33, §33.1.1-33.1.3, printed pp. 258-260 (specialization v=1, Serre quotient = f, dimension comparison, Theorem 33.1.3(d)).

contents.name: Ch. 1, §1.2.3, Proposition (printed p. 4): existence, uniqueness and symmetry of the inner product on the free algebra with (1,1)=1 and prescribed values on the generators; §1.2.4 (the radical is a two-sided ideal)

Ch. 1, §1.2.5, §1.2.12 and §1.2.15 (printed pp. 5, 6, 9): the quotient f by the radical, non-degeneracy on each homogeneous piece, and the separation statement (if r_i(x)=0 for all i and x in f_nu with nu non-zero then x=0)
Ch. 1, §1.2.13-1.2.14 (printed p. 8): the skew derivations r_i and bar r_i with twisted Leibniz rules, their adjunction against left multiplication by theta_i, and the bar compatibility

Ch. 23, §23.1.3, identity (6) (printed p. 186): the divided-power reordering with toral quantum binomials in the modified algebra, and §23.2.1-23.2.2 (printed p. 188): triangular decomposition and A-basis of the A-form
Ch. 23, §23.2.1-23.2.2 (printed p. 188) and Ch. 31, §31.1 (printed pp. 245-246): triangularity of the A-form, its generators and its A-basis

Ch. 33, §33.1.1-33.1.3 (printed pp. 258-260): the specialization v=1 of the Serre-presented half, the identification of R_0 f with the enveloping algebra of the triangular part of the Kac-Moody Lie algebra, and the degreewise dimension comparison of Theorem 33.1.3(a),(b)

Ch. 33, §33.1.2-33.1.3, Theorem 33.1.3(d) (printed pp. 259-260): equality of the weight multiplicities of the integrable highest weight module with those of the simple integrable highest weight representation of the Kac-Moody Lie algebra, for regular root data

Ch. 3, §3.1 (printed pp. 16-25): presentation of U by generators, the Chevalley involutions and the Hopf structure; §3.5 with the highest weight modules and integrability conditions F_i^{(lambda(h_i)+1)}v=0
Ch. 3, §3.4-3.5 (printed pp. 27-38): duality and the contravariant form on integrable highest weight modules
Ch. 34-35, §34.1, §35.1 (printed pp. 265-269): Gaussian binomials and the Frobenius-type behaviour at roots of unity
contents.reason: Root-of-unity phenomena (quantum Frobenius, the small quantum group and the l-divided-power identities) are outside this pair's scope: the page works over Q(q) with q transcendental and needs only the q=1 specialization, not specialization to a root of unity.

contents.name: Ch. 4-5 (printed pp. 39-56): the algebra f as a self-dual braided Hopf algebra, the canonical basis constructions and the Kashiwara operators on f
contents.reason: The crystal operators, the crystal lattices L(Lambda) and the grand loop belong to the QG-3 pair, which declares them separately; this pair records only the skew derivations, the form and the nondegeneracy joint they supply.

contents.name: Ch. 14 and Ch. 25-26 (canonical bases and the modified algebra U-dot): the canonical basis, its integrality and the A-form of the modified algebra
contents.reason: Canonical/global bases and their categorification statements are declared by QG-5 and QG-7; the negative half form proved here is the input those pages consume, and no canonical basis claim is made on this page.

contents.name: §1, printed p. 5, display (1.5) and §1
§6, printed pp. 22-23, displays (6.1)-(6.3): the unique decomposition e_iP-Pe_i=(K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R)/(q_i-q_i^{-1}) and the definition and commutation relations of e_i' and e_i''

§6, printed p. 23, displays (6.5)-(6.6) and Proposition 6.1: existence of the unique nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form with (1,1)=1 and (f_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'Q), its behaviour under the anti-involution, and the i-string decomposition with the projection P_i
§2, printed p. 8, display (2.1) and Proposition 2.2: for lambda in P^+ the highest weight vector of V(lambda) satisfies f_i^{lambda(h_i)+1}v_lambda=0, and conversely

§2, printed p. 8, displays (2.2)-(2.3) with Lemma 2.3: the anti-involution e_i -> q_i f_i K_i^{-1}, f_i -> q_i^{-1}K_i e_i, the unique symmetric bilinear form on V(lambda) with (v_lambda,v_lambda)=1 and its nondegeneracy
§3, printed pp. 10-13, Definition 3.1, Lemma 3.6 and Theorem 3.7: the category O_int, the splitting of a highest weight submodule generated by a maximal vector, and complete reducibility
§3, printed p. 11, Propositions 3.3-3.4: a highest weight module in O_int has highest weight in P^+ and is isomorphic to V(lambda)
§3-§9 (crystal bases for U_q^- and for modules, global bases): the crystal lattice and crystal basis theory built on the §6 operators
contents.reason: The crystal basis theory for the negative half and for integrable modules is the declared content of the QG-3 and QG-4 pairs; this pair builds only the skew derivations, form and nondegeneracy on which those pages depend.

contents.name: §1-§2, Borcherds-Cartan generality (imaginary simple roots, a_ii<=0 cases of (2.1), (6.4))
contents.reason: The library's Cartan datum is a generalized Cartan matrix with a_ii=2 for all i, so the imaginary-simple-root branches of the generalized Kac-Moody theory are not part of this page's scope and are not asserted.
